sanskrit: annaṃ prāṇā narāṇāṃ hi sarvam anne pratiṣṭhitam annadaḥ paśumān putrī dhanavān bhogavān api
english: Food is the very life-breath of men, for all things rest upon food. The giver of food becomes rich in cattle, blessed with sons, abounding in wealth, and full of enjoyments.

sanskrit: prāṇavāṃś cāpi bhavati rūpavāṃś ca tathā nṛpa annadaḥ prāṇado loke sarvadaḥ procyate tu saḥ
english: He becomes vigorous in life and comely in form as well, O king. The giver of food is in this world a giver of life, and he is called the giver of all things.

sanskrit: annaṃ hi dattvātithaye brāhmaṇāya yathāvidhi pradātā sukham āpnoti devaiś cāpy abhipūjyate
english: For when one bestows food, according to the ordinance, upon a guest who is a brāhmaṇa, the giver attains happiness and is honored even by the gods.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇo hi mahad bhūtaṃ kṣetraṃ carati pādavat upyate tatra yad bījaṃ tad dhi puṇyaphalaṃ mahat
english: The brāhmaṇa is indeed a great being who roams about as a field on foot; and whatever seed is sown therein yields a mighty fruit of merit.

sanskrit: pratyakṣaṃ prītijananaṃ bhoktṛdātror bhavaty uta sarvāṇy anyāni dānāni parokṣaphalavanty uta
english: The gift of food brings joy at once, plainly visible, both to him who eats and to him who gives; whereas all other gifts bear their fruit only out of sight.

sanskrit: annād dhi prasavaṃ viddhi ratim annād dhi bhārata dharmārthāv annato viddhi roganāśaṃ tathānnataḥ
english: Know that procreation springs from food, and from food too comes delight, O Bhārata. Know that dharma and prosperity arise from food, and likewise from food comes the destruction of disease.

sanskrit: annaṃ hy amṛtam ity āha purākalpe prajāpatiḥ annaṃ bhuvaṃ divaṃ khaṃ ca sarvam anne pratiṣṭhitam
english: In the ancient age Prajāpati declared that food is verily ambrosia. Food is the earth, the heaven, and the sky; all things rest upon food.

sanskrit: annapraṇāśe bhidyante śarīre pañca dhātavaḥ balaṃ balavato 'pīha praṇaśyaty annahānitaḥ
english: When food is wanting, the five elements within the body fall asunder; and the strength even of the strong perishes in this world through lack of food.

sanskrit: āvāhāś ca vivāhāś ca yajñāś cānnam ṛte tathā na vartante naraśreṣṭha brahma cātra pralīyate
english: Receptions and weddings and sacrifices cannot proceed without food, O best of men, and the recitation of the Veda too dissolves away for want of it.

sanskrit: annataḥ sarvam etad dhi yat kiṃ cit sthāṇu jaṅgamam triṣu lokeṣu dharmārtham annaṃ deyam ato budhaiḥ
english: For all this, whatever is fixed or moving, arises from food. Therefore, throughout the three worlds, food should be given by the wise for the sake of dharma.

sanskrit: annadasya manuṣyasya balam ojo yaśaḥ sukham kīrtiś ca vardhate śaśvat triṣu lokeṣu pārthiva
english: For the man who gives food, his strength, vigor, glory, happiness, and renown grow forever throughout the three worlds, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: megheṣv ambhaḥ saṃnidhatte prāṇānāṃ pavanaḥ śivaḥ tac ca meghagataṃ vāri śakro varṣati bhārata
english: The auspicious wind, the very breath of living things, gathers water in the clouds; and that water lodged within the clouds Śakra rains down, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: ādatte ca rasaṃ bhaumam ādityaḥ svagabhastibhiḥ vāyur ādityatas tāṃś ca rasān devaḥ prajāpatiḥ
english: And Āditya, the sun, draws up the moisture of the earth with his own rays; and from the sun the wind, the god Prajāpati, draws those essences.

sanskrit: tad yadā meghato vāri patitaṃ bhavati kṣitau tadā vasumatī devī snigdhā bhavati bhārata
english: And when the water has fallen from the cloud upon the ground, then the goddess Earth, bearer of treasures, grows moist and rich, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tataḥ sasyāni rohanti yena vartayate jagat māṃsamedosthiśukrāṇāṃ prādurbhāvas tataḥ punaḥ
english: Thereupon the crops spring up, by which the world is sustained; and from that, in turn, arises the production of flesh, fat, bone, and seed.

sanskrit: saṃbhavanti tataḥ śukrāt prāṇinaḥ pṛthivīpate agnīṣomau hi tac chukraṃ prajanaḥ puṣyataś ca ha
english: Then from that seed living creatures come into being, O lord of the earth; for Agni and Soma are that generative seed, and they nourish the begetting of offspring.

sanskrit: evam annaṃ ca sūryaś ca pavanaḥ śukram eva ca eka eva smṛto rāśir yato bhūtāni jajñire
english: Thus food, and the sun, and the wind, and the seed are remembered as one single mass, from which all beings have been born.

sanskrit: prāṇān dadāti bhūtānāṃ tejaś ca bharatarṣabha gṛham abhyāgatāyāśu yo dadyād annam arthine
english: He who promptly gives food to a needy one come to his house bestows life-breath upon living beings, and splendor as well, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca nāradenaivam ukto 'ham adām annaṃ sadā nṛpa anasūyus tvam apy annaṃ tasmād dehi gatajvaraḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus addressed by Nārada, I gave food always, O king. Do you too, free of envy and freed of all fever of heart, give food therefore.

sanskrit: dattvānnaṃ vidhivad rājan viprebhyas tvam api prabho yathāvad anurūpebhyas tataḥ svargam avāpsyasi
english: Having given food according to the ordinance, O king, to brāhmaṇas worthy of it and as is fitting, O lord, you too shall thereby attain heaven.

sanskrit: annadānāṃ hi ye lokās tāṃs tvaṃ śṛṇu narādhipa bhavanāni prakāśante divi teṣāṃ mahātmanām nānāsaṃsthānarūpāṇi nānāstambhānvitāni ca
english: Now hear of those worlds that belong to the givers of food, O ruler of men. In heaven there shine the mansions of those great-souled ones, of manifold shapes and forms and furnished with manifold pillars.

sanskrit: candramaṇḍalaśubhrāṇi kiṅkiṇījālavanti ca taruṇādityavarṇāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca
english: White as the orb of the moon, hung with nets of little bells, of the hue of the young rising sun, some standing fixed and some that move.

sanskrit: anekaśatabhaumāni sāntarjalavanāni ca vaiḍūryārkaprakāśāni raupyarukmamayāni ca
english: Rising in many hundreds of storeys, having within them pools of water and groves, gleaming like beryl and the sun, and wrought of silver and gold.

sanskrit: sarvakāmaphalāś cāpi vṛkṣā bhavanasaṃsthitāḥ vāpyo vīthyaḥ sabhāḥ kūpā dīrghikāś caiva sarvaśaḥ
english: And trees yielding the fruit of every desire stand set within those mansions, with tanks, avenues, halls, wells, and long ponds on every side.

sanskrit: ghoṣavanti ca yānāni yuktāny atha sahasraśaḥ bhakṣyabhojyamayāḥ śailā vāsāṃsy ābharaṇāni ca
english: And resounding chariots stand ready harnessed by the thousand; there are mountains made of dainties and viands, and garments and ornaments too.

sanskrit: kṣīraṃ sravantyaḥ saritas tathā caivānnaparvatāḥ prāsādāḥ pāṇḍurābhrābhāḥ śayyāś ca kanakojjvalāḥ tān annadāḥ prapadyante tasmād annaprado bhava
english: There are rivers streaming with milk, and mountains of food, palaces gleaming like pale white clouds, and couches bright with gold. To these the givers of food attain; therefore be a giver of food.

sanskrit: ete lokāḥ puṇyakṛtām annadānāṃ mahātmanām tasmād annaṃ viśeṣeṇa dātavyaṃ mānavair bhuvi
english: These are the worlds of those great-souled doers of meritorious deeds, the givers of food. Therefore food above all should be given by men upon the earth.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca śrutaṃ me bhavato vākyam annadānasya yo vidhiḥ nakṣatrayogasyedānīṃ dānakalpaṃ bravīhi me
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: I have heard your words on the rule for the giving of food. Now tell me of the manner of giving according to the conjunction of the lunar mansions.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam devakyāś caiva saṃvādaṃ devarṣer nāradasya ca
english: Bhīṣma said: On this point too they recount this ancient tale, the dialogue between Devakī and the divine sage Nārada.

sanskrit: dvārakām anusaṃprāptaṃ nāradaṃ devadarśanam papracchainaṃ tataḥ praśnaṃ devakī dharmadarśinī
english: When Nārada, who beheld the gods, had come to Dvārakā, Devakī, who looked upon dharma, then put this question to him.

sanskrit: tasyāḥ saṃpṛcchamānāyā devarṣir nāradas tadā ācaṣṭa vidhivat sarvaṃ yat tac chṛṇu viśāṃ pate
english: To her as she questioned, the divine sage Nārada then expounded all duly, according to the ordinance. Hear that, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca kṛttikāsu mahābhāge pāyasena sasarpiṣā saṃtarpya brāhmaṇān sādhūṃl lokān āpnoty anuttamān
english: Nārada said: Under the asterism Kṛttikā, O blessed lady, by satisfying worthy brāhmaṇas with milk-rice mixed with ghee, one attains worlds most excellent.

sanskrit: rohiṇyāṃ prathitair māṃsair māṣair annena sarpiṣā payo 'nupānaṃ dātavyam ānṛṇyārthaṃ dvijātaye
english: Under Rohiṇī one should give to a twice-born, for the sake of discharging one's debt, choice meats, beans, cooked food, and ghee, with milk to drink afterward.

sanskrit: dogdhrīṃ dattvā savatsāṃ tu nakṣatre somadaivate gacchanti mānuṣāl lokāt svargalokam anuttamam
english: Having given a milch cow together with her calf under the asterism whose deity is Soma, men pass from the world of men to the most excellent world of heaven.

sanskrit: ārdrāyāṃ kṛsaraṃ dattvā tailamiśram upoṣitaḥ naras tarati durgāṇi kṣuradhārāṃś ca parvatān
english: Having fasted and given, under Ārdrā, a dish of rice and sesame mingled with oil, a man crosses over difficult straits and mountains sharp as razors' edges.

sanskrit: apūpān punarvasau dattvā tathaivānnāni śobhane yaśasvī rūpasaṃpanno bahvanne jāyate kule
english: Having given cakes and likewise foods under the fair asterism Punarvasu, one is born renowned and endowed with beauty in a house abounding in food.

sanskrit: puṣye tu kanakaṃ dattvā kṛtaṃ cākṛtam eva ca anālokeṣu lokeṣu somavat sa virājate
english: Having given gold under Puṣya, whether wrought or unwrought, he shines like the moon in worlds that are otherwise without light.

sanskrit: āśleṣāyāṃ tu yo rūpyam ṛṣabhaṃ vā prayacchati sa sarvabhayanirmuktaḥ śātravān adhitiṣṭhati
english: He who under Āśleṣā gives silver or a bull becomes freed from every fear and stands triumphant over his foes.

sanskrit: maghāsu tilapūrṇāni vardhamānāni mānavaḥ pradāya putrapaśumān iha pretya ca modate
english: Having presented under Maghā vessels filled with sesame, brimming over, a man, blessed with sons and cattle, rejoices both here and in the world to come.

sanskrit: phalgunīpūrvasamaye brāhmaṇānām upoṣitaḥ bhakṣān phāṇitasaṃyuktān dattvā saubhāgyam ṛcchati
english: At the season of the Pūrvā Phālgunī, having fasted and given to brāhmaṇas dainties prepared with raw sugar, one attains good fortune.

sanskrit: ghṛtakṣīrasamāyuktaṃ vidhivat ṣaṣṭikaudanam uttarāviṣaye dattvā svargaloke mahīyate
english: Having given duly, in the domain of the Uttarā asterism, rice of the sixty-day kind dressed with ghee and milk, one is exalted in the world of heaven.

sanskrit: yad yat pradīyate dānam uttarāviṣaye naraiḥ mahāphalam anantaṃ ca bhavatīti viniścayaḥ
english: Whatever gift is bestowed by men in the domain of the Uttarā asterism becomes of great and endless fruit: such is the settled truth.

sanskrit: haste hastirathaṃ dattvā caturyuktam upoṣitaḥ prāpnoti paramāṃl lokān puṇyakāmasamanvitān
english: Having fasted and given under Hasta an elephant-chariot drawn by four, one attains the highest worlds, fulfilled in merit and in desire.

sanskrit: citrāyām ṛṣabhaṃ dattvā puṇyān gandhāṃś ca bhārata caraty apsarasāṃ loke ramate nandane tathā
english: Having given under Citrā a bull and holy perfumes, O Bhārata, one roams in the world of the apsarases and takes delight in the grove of Nandana.

sanskrit: svātāv atha dhanaṃ dattvā yad iṣṭatamam ātmanaḥ prāpnoti lokān sa śubhān iha caiva mahad yaśaḥ
english: And having given under Svāti the wealth that is dearest to himself, he attains auspicious worlds, and great renown even here.

sanskrit: viśākhāyām anaḍvāhaṃ dhenuṃ dattvā ca dugdhadām saprāsaṅgaṃ ca śakaṭaṃ sadhānyaṃ vastrasaṃyutam
english: Under Viśākhā, having given an ox and a milch cow yielding milk, and a cart with its yoke-pole, laden with grain and furnished with cloth—

sanskrit: pitṝn devāṃś ca prīṇāti pretya cānantyam aśnute na ca durgāṇy avāpnoti svargalokaṃ ca gacchati
english: —he gladdens the ancestors and the gods, and after death enjoys the endless; he meets with no hard straits and goes to the world of heaven.

sanskrit: dattvā yathoktaṃ viprebhyo vṛttim iṣṭāṃ sa vindati narakādīṃś ca saṃkleśān nāpnotīti viniścayaḥ
english: Having given to brāhmaṇas as prescribed, he obtains the livelihood he desires, and does not meet with hell and other torments: such is the settled truth.

sanskrit: anurādhāsu prāvāraṃ vastrāntaram upoṣitaḥ dattvā yugaśataṃ cāpi naraḥ svarge mahīyate
english: Having fasted and given under Anurādhā an outer wrap and another garment, a man is exalted in heaven for even a hundred ages.

sanskrit: kālaśākaṃ tu viprebhyo dattvā martyaḥ samūlakam jyeṣṭhāyām ṛddhim iṣṭāṃ vai gatim iṣṭāṃ ca vindati
english: A mortal who under Jyeṣṭhā gives to brāhmaṇas dark pot-herbs together with their roots gains the prosperity he wishes for and the destiny he desires.

sanskrit: mūle mūlaphalaṃ dattvā brāhmaṇebhyaḥ samāhitaḥ pitṝn prīṇayate cāpi gatim iṣṭāṃ ca gacchati
english: Having given roots and fruits to brāhmaṇas under Mūla with a composed mind, he gladdens the ancestors and goes to the destiny he desires.

sanskrit: atha pūrvāsv aṣāḍhāsu dadhipātrāṇy upoṣitaḥ kulavṛttopasaṃpanne brāhmaṇe vedapārage pradāya jāyate pretya kule subahugokule
english: And under the Pūrvā Aṣāḍhā, having fasted, by presenting bowls of curds to a brāhmaṇa endowed with good family conduct and versed to the end in the Veda, one is born after death into a house rich in herds of cattle.

sanskrit: udamanthaṃ sasarpiṣkaṃ prabhūtamadhuphāṇitam dattvottarāsv aṣāḍhāsu sarvakāmān avāpnuyāt
english: Having given under the Uttarā Aṣāḍhā a barley-and-water gruel with ghee and abundant honey and raw sugar, one would attain all desires.

sanskrit: dugdhaṃ tv abhijite yoge dattvā madhughṛtāplutam dharmanityo manīṣibhyaḥ svargaloke mahīyate
english: And one ever devoted to dharma who, under the conjunction of Abhijit, gives to the wise milk drenched with honey and ghee is exalted in the world of heaven.

sanskrit: śravaṇe kambalaṃ dattvā vastrāntaritam eva ca śvetena yāti yānena sarvalokān asaṃvṛtān
english: Having given under Śravaṇa a woolen blanket together with another garment, one journeys in a white chariot through all the unobstructed worlds.

sanskrit: goprayuktaṃ dhaniṣṭhāsu yānaṃ dattvā samāhitaḥ vastraraśmidharaṃ sadyaḥ pretya rājyaṃ prapadyate
english: Having given under Dhaniṣṭhā with composed mind an ox-drawn carriage fitted with cloth and reins, he straightway attains sovereignty after death.

sanskrit: gandhāñ śatabhiṣagyoge dattvā sāgurucandanān prāpnoty apsarasāṃ lokān pretya gandhāṃś ca śāśvatān
english: Having given under the conjunction of Śatabhiṣaj perfumes together with aloe-wood and sandal, one attains after death the worlds of the apsarases and fragrances everlasting.

sanskrit: pūrvabhādrapadāyoge rājamāṣān pradāya tu sarvabhakṣaphalopetaḥ sa vai pretya sukhī bhavet
english: And having presented kidney-beans under the conjunction of Pūrvā Bhādrapadā, endowed with the fruit of every kind of food, he is verily happy after death.

sanskrit: aurabhram uttarāyoge yas tu māṃsaṃ prayacchati sa pitṝn prīṇayati vai pretya cānantyam aśnute
english: He who under the conjunction of Uttarā Bhādrapadā gives the flesh of a ram gladdens the ancestors and after death enjoys the endless.

sanskrit: kāṃsyopadohanāṃ dhenuṃ revatyāṃ yaḥ prayacchati sā pretya kāmān ādāya dātāram upatiṣṭhati
english: He who under Revatī gives a milch cow milked into a bronze vessel—after death she comes, bearing his desires, and waits upon the giver.

sanskrit: ratham aśvasamāyuktaṃ dattvāśvinyāṃ narottamaḥ hastyaśvarathasaṃpanne varcasvī jāyate kule
english: Having given under Aśvinī a chariot yoked with horses, the best of men is born radiant in a house rich in elephants, horses, and chariots.

sanskrit: bharaṇīṣu dvijātibhyas tiladhenuṃ pradāya vai gāḥ suprabhūtāḥ prāpnoti naraḥ pretya yaśas tathā
english: Having presented under Bharaṇī to twice-born ones a cow made of sesame, a man obtains cattle in great abundance, and renown likewise, after death.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ity eṣa lakṣaṇoddeśaḥ prokto nakṣatrayogataḥ devakyā nāradeneha sā snuṣābhyo 'bravīd idam
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus was this summary of the marks declared, according to the conjunction of the lunar mansions, by Nārada to Devakī; and she spoke this to her daughters-in-law.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca sarvān kāmān prayacchanti ye prayacchanti kāñcanam ity evaṃ bhagavān atriḥ pitāmahasuto 'bravīt
english: Bhīṣma said: Those who give gold give all desires—thus spoke the venerable Atri, the son of the Grandsire.

sanskrit: pavitraṃ śucy athāyuṣyaṃ pitṝṇām akṣayaṃ ca tat suvarṇaṃ manujendreṇa hariścandreṇa kīrtitam
english: Gold is purifying, pure, life-giving, and, for the ancestors, imperishable—so it was extolled by Hariścandra, the lord of men.

sanskrit: pānīyadānaṃ paramaṃ dānānāṃ manur abravīt tasmād vāpīś ca kūpāṃś ca taḍāgāni ca khānayet
english: The gift of water is the highest of gifts, Manu declared. Therefore one should have tanks and wells and pools dug out.

sanskrit: ardhaṃ pāpasya harati puruṣasyeha karmaṇaḥ kūpaḥ pravṛttapānīyaḥ supravṛttaś ca nityaśaḥ
english: A well whose water flows freely and ever flows well carries away here half the sin of a man's deeds.

sanskrit: sarvaṃ tārayate vaṃśaṃ yasya khāte jalāśaye gāvaḥ pibanti viprāś ca sādhavaś ca narāḥ sadā
english: He whose dug-out reservoir is one where cattle and brāhmaṇas and good men ever drink saves his whole lineage.

sanskrit: nidāghakāle pānīyaṃ yasya tiṣṭhaty avāritam sa durgaṃ viṣamaṃ kṛcchraṃ na kadā cid avāpnute
english: He at whose place water stands unstinted in the season of summer's heat never meets with hardship, peril, or distress.

sanskrit: bṛhaspater bhagavataḥ pūṣṇaś caiva bhagasya ca aśvinoś caiva vahneś ca prītir bhavati sarpiṣā
english: By the gift of ghee there comes the favor of the venerable Bṛhaspati, of Pūṣan, of Bhaga, of the two Aśvins, and of the Fire.

sanskrit: paramaṃ bheṣajaṃ hy etad yajñānām etad uttamam rasānām uttamaṃ caitat phalānāṃ caitad uttamam
english: For this ghee is the supreme medicine; this is the best of offerings in sacrifice; this is the best of savory things and the best of fruits.

sanskrit: phalakāmo yaśaskāmaḥ puṣṭikāmaś ca nityadā ghṛtaṃ dadyād dvijātibhyaḥ puruṣaḥ śucir ātmavān
english: He who desires fruit, who desires fame, and who desires thriving—such a man, pure and self-possessed, should ever give ghee to the twice-born.

sanskrit: ghṛtaṃ māse āśvayuji viprebhyo yaḥ prayacchati tasmai prayacchato rūpaṃ prītau devāv ihāśvinau
english: For him who gives ghee to brāhmaṇas in the month of Āśvayuja, the two Aśvin gods, well pleased, bestow beauty in this world.

sanskrit: pāyasaṃ sarpiṣā miśraṃ dvijebhyo yaḥ prayacchati gṛhaṃ tasya na rakṣāṃsi dharṣayanti kadā cana
english: He who gives to the twice-born milk-rice mixed with ghee—his house the rākṣasas never assail at any time.

sanskrit: pipāsayā na mriyate sopacchandaś ca dṛśyate na prāpnuyāc ca vyasanaṃ karakān yaḥ prayacchati
english: He who gives waterpots does not die of thirst, is seen to be pleasing of speech, and meets with no calamity.

sanskrit: prayato brāhmaṇāgrebhyaḥ śraddhayā parayā yutaḥ upasparśanaṣaḍbhāgaṃ labhate puruṣaḥ sadā
english: The man who, self-restrained and filled with supreme faith, gives to the foremost of brāhmaṇas obtains ever a sixth share of the merit of their ritual sippings of water.

sanskrit: yaḥ sādhanārthaṃ kāṣṭhāni brāhmaṇebhyaḥ prayacchati pratāpārthaṃ ca rājendra vṛttavadbhyaḥ sadā naraḥ
english: The man who, for the sake of their rites and for warmth, ever gives firewood to brāhmaṇas of good conduct, O king of kings—

sanskrit: sidhyanty arthāḥ sadā tasya kāryāṇi vividhāni ca upary upari śatrūṇāṃ vapuṣā dīpyate ca saḥ
english: —for him his aims ever prosper and his manifold undertakings as well; and he blazes in splendor of form higher and higher above his foes.

sanskrit: bhagavāṃś cāsya suprīto vahnir bhavati nityaśaḥ na taṃ tyajante paśavaḥ saṃgrāme ca jayaty api
english: And the venerable Fire is ever well pleased with him; the herds do not forsake him, and in battle too he is victorious.

sanskrit: putrāñ chriyaṃ ca labhate yaś chatraṃ saṃprayacchati cakṣurvyādhiṃ na labhate yajñabhāgam athāśnute
english: He who gives a parasol obtains sons and prosperity; he contracts no disease of the eyes, and he partakes of a share in the sacrifice.
